claim: Unlocked BF16 tensor throughput on the CMP 170HX measures 164.4-192.7 TFLOPS with a 202.1 TFLOPS ceiling, against 6.41 TFLOPS locked — a ~28x unlock.
stance_target: The repo's hardware-table claim of bf16 ~162 TFLOPS per GPU and ~810 TFLOPS for 5 cards
scope_conditions: Compute-unlocked cards at stock clocks; cuBLAS tensor tests and torch GEMM sweeps
quoted_support: BF16 tensor | 6.41 TFLOPS | 164.4-192.7 TFLOPS | ~28x | ceiling 202.1 TFLOPS

claim: The repo's bf16 ~162 TFLOPS figure sits at the low end of the measured 164.4-192.7 TFLOPS band, so the headline ~810 TFLOPS for 5 cards is conservative: the same measurements support up to ~963 TFLOPS.
stance_target: The repo's ~810 TFLOPS bf16 headline for the 5-card box
quoted_support: BF16 tensor | 6.41 TFLOPS | 164.4-192.7 TFLOPS | ~28x | ceiling 202.1 TFLOPS

claim: FP4, FP6 and FP8 MMA are not supported on the CMP 170HX, described as 'expected for sm_80'.
stance_target: The repo's claim that GA100 has no FP8 tensor cores, which rules out FP8 training recipes
scope_conditions: Per-instruction MMA microbenchmarks on unlocked cards
quoted_support: FP4 / FP6 / FP8 MMA | not supported | not supported | n/a | expected for sm_80

claim: FP32 non-tensor throughput unlocks from 0.30-0.41 TFLOPS to 12.58 TFLOPS (28-31x), and FP64 non-tensor runs at exactly half of FP32 (6.223-6.31 TFLOPS), the full unrestricted GA100 rate.
stance_target: The repo's claim that fp32 is only ~13 TFLOPS and that bf16 autocast is mandatory
scope_conditions: Compute-unlocked cards at stock clocks; 1024/4096/8192 modded sweeps, gpu-burn, clpeak, OpenCL-Benchmark
quoted_support: FP32 non-tensor | 0.30 / 0.40 / 0.41 TFLOPS | 12.58 TFLOPS | 28.4x-30.7x ... FP64 non-tensor | 0.20 TFLOPS | 6.223-6.31 TFLOPS | ~31x | 1/2 of FP32, the full unrestricted GA100 rate

claim: TF32 tensor throughput measures 79-94 TFLOPS unlocked, the widest spread of any datatype, against 2.96-3.21 TFLOPS locked.
scope_conditions: 8 rented cards plus modded sweeps and mma.sync microbenchmarks
quoted_support: TF32 tensor | 2.96-3.21 TFLOPS | 79-94 TFLOPS | 15x-28x | widest spread of any datatype

claim: HBM bandwidth has no single canonical value: measured spans 1305.86 GB/s to 1600 GB/s, with a theoretical peak of 1555.2 GB/s (1215 MHz DDR x 5120-bit = 1448.4 GiB/s), and stock-vs-modded on the same card is 1592 -> 1599 GB/s (1.0x).
stance_target: The repo's memory-bandwidth assumptions for roofline and activation-size arithmetic
scope_conditions: 8 rented 64 GB cards, OpenCL coalesced/misaligned patterns, 256 MB working set; the page warns to quote the range not a point estimate
quoted_support: Measured HBM bandwidth spans 1305.86 GB/s to 1600 GB/s and no methodology reconciles the range. ... Quote the range, not a point estimate.

claim: PCIe bandwidth by link configuration: Gen1 x4 ~0.85 GB/s (clpeak, high confidence); Gen1 x4 under inference load ~1.0 GB/s and did not ramp; Gen1 x16 cap-mod-only 2.88 GB/s; Gen2 x4 send 1.68 / receive 1.71 GB/s; Gen2 x16 branch plus full 24-capacitor mod 6.63-6.67 GB/s (~83% of the 8 GB/s line rate).
stance_target: The repo's ~0.75 GiB/s all-reduce figure, which is consistent with a Gen2 x4 link and would be ~4x higher at Gen2 x16
scope_conditions: clpeak, OpenCL-Benchmark, ocl_pcie_bw; two rigs have published Gen2 x16 captures
quoted_support: Gen2 x16 | branch and full 24-capacitor mod | 6.63-6.67 GB/s (~83% of the 8 GB/s line rate); nvtop TX 7.061 GiB/s | ocl_pcie_bw | medium

claim: Gen2 x16 has two published captures — 6.63-6.67 GB/s on one card on 2026-07-26 and 5.97 GB/s on each of four cards with zero AER errors over 90 minutes — but nobody has published a long burn-in.
stance_target: How much confidence to place in a Gen2 x16 plan
scope_conditions: Two independent rigs; no long-duration burn-in published
quoted_support: Two rigs have published captures: 6.63 to 6.67 GB/s on one card on 2026-07-26, and 5.97 GB/s on each of four cards with zero AER errors over 90 minutes. Nobody has published a long burn-in.

claim: PCIe sensitivity is topology-dependent: single-card llama.cpp x4->x16 moves throughput only ~+2% (pp 439->448, tg 81.91->85.75), while three-card CPU-offload prefill moves +44.2% (pp2048 33.44->48.22 t/s) — but that row's post-Gen2 run used a Q4-labelled quant where the pre-Gen2 run was unlabelled, so the delta may be overstated.
stance_target: Whether the box's slow link actually binds a given workload, which depends on whether weights are resident
scope_conditions: llama.cpp and ik_llama runs; single-card fully-VRAM-resident model versus three-card CPU-offload; same tester for two rows, no independent Gen2 x4 inference measurement
quoted_support: The reconciliation: single-card work is largely bandwidth-local (weights are resident, only the model load crosses the link), while multi-card and CPU-offload prefill is link-bound.

claim: A single-card Gen1 x4 -> Gen2 x4 comparison on a fully VRAM-resident Qwen3.6-27B-MTP-UD-Q8_K_XL moved pp2048 from 328.81 to 449.41 t/s and pp8192 from 363.25 to 493.86, a change neither the tester nor the channel could explain for a resident model.
stance_target: Whether link speed affects compute-bound single-card work at all — an unresolved anomaly
scope_conditions: ik_llama with MTP, model fully VRAM-resident, same tester five days apart, 'all other factors unchanged'
quoted_support: The single-card row complicates the picture rather than settling it: that model was entirely resident in VRAM, and neither the tester nor anyone in the channel could explain why the link speed moved it at all.

claim: Nobody has measured Gen2 x16 on a multi-card LLM rig: the Gen2 x16 bandwidth figure and the Gen1-to-Gen2 inference runs were measured on different systems and never combined.
stance_target: Whether a Gen2 x16 plan for the 5-card box can be justified from existing evidence
scope_conditions: Stated open problem; the 2x2 matrix of {Gen1,Gen2} x {x4,x16} on one rig with one model would settle it
quoted_support: Open problem: nobody has measured Gen2 x16 on a multi-card LLM rig. The Gen2 x16 bandwidth figure and the Gen1-to-Gen2 inference runs were measured on different systems and never combined.

claim: The performance page contains no training, fine-tuning, pretraining, all-reduce, NCCL, DDP or gradient-communication measurement at all — every number is inference or microbenchmark.
stance_target: Any assumption that the repo's DDP overhead model (~20% at 1M-token batches, ~0.75 GiB/s all-reduce) is corroborated by the hardware wiki
quoted_support: What this page covers. Every reproducible throughput number for the CMP 170HX: compute rates per datatype before and after the unlock, HBM bandwidth, PCIe bandwidth at each link configuration

claim: The compute unlock is a register write, not a clock change, and it does not touch power limit or PCIe link speed, so every measured figure is a stock-clock figure.
stance_target: Whether the measured TFLOPS numbers are achievable without overclocking or power-modding the cards
quoted_support: The compute unlock is a register write, not a clock change. Writing ... takes FP32 from 0.30-0.41 TFLOPS to 12.2-12.8 TFLOPS ... power limit or PCIe link speed, so every figure below is a stock-clock figure unless it says otherwise.
